# Six-Hops Reachability Audit - 2026-05-20

Audit-only artifact for the Markdown corpus under `docs/` and `microservices/`.
The audit checks whether every Markdown file is reachable from `docs/README.md` in <=6 directed Markdown-link hops, and separately records the <=3-hop warning band cited by the synthesis adjudication §13.3.
Because this report is itself a Markdown file under `docs/architecture/`, the post-write graph includes this audit artifact as a node. The audit-only constraint forbids adding a source index link to it in this change.

## §1 Methodology

| Rule | Applied semantics |
|---|---|
| Node set | Every filesystem `*.md` file under `/Users/jasonlee/oyatie/docs/` and `/Users/jasonlee/oyatie/microservices/`, normalized as repo-relative POSIX paths. |
| Start node | `docs/README.md`; hop distance 0. |
| Link syntax | Inline Markdown links with bracketed text and a parenthesized target were scanned across the full file text. Image links were ignored. Reference-style links and frontmatter path fields were not treated as graph edges. |
| Relative path rule | Only relative targets participate. External URLs, URI schemes, protocol-relative URLs, root-absolute paths, anchor-only links, self-links, and unresolved/out-of-corpus links were skipped. |
| Fragment/query handling | Fragment and query suffixes were stripped before path resolution. Fragments do not create separate nodes. |
| Directory links | A relative directory target resolves to `README.md` first, then `INDEX.md`, if either exists as a corpus node. Extensionless file targets also try `.md`. |
| Edge direction | Directed edge from the file containing the link to the resolved target file. BFS follows edge direction. |
| Duplicate links | Multiple links from the same source to the same target collapse into one edge for traversal and in-degree counts. |
| Microservice grouping | A microservice row is the second path segment under `microservices/<service>/...`. |
| Component catalogue | Weak components are computed over resolved corpus edges for diagnosis, but pass/fail uses directed BFS from `docs/README.md`. |

Graph construction was computed with an ephemeral Python traversal over the live workspace. No persisted source script was added. The only authored file is this audit report.

## §6 Recommended Remediation

Ranking method: for each currently unreachable file, the audit simulated adding one direct index/cross-reference from a reachable hub to that file, then counted how many currently unreachable files would become reachable within the remaining five hops using existing outgoing links. High-gain rows are better hub targets. Preferred implementation pattern is to add a small `docs/README.md` or Tier-1 docs link to a microservices index, then link that index to service `README.md`/`PRD.md`/`ARCHITECTURE.md` hubs, instead of stuffing every leaf file into the root README.
